about.title: Brea Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Brea's mix of warehouses, retail centers, and office parks near SR-57 and Imperial Highway means workplace injuries here range from forklift accidents to slip-and-falls in commercial spaces. Orange County's workers' comp system is usually the first stop after a job injury, covering medical care and partial wage replacement regardless of fault. But it's not the whole picture. If a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer contributed to what happened, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your comp benefits. Brea's workforce, spread across logistics, retail, and service industries, faces a variety of on-the-job risks, and figuring out whether an outside party bears responsibility isn't always straightforward. LawProactive doesn't practice law, but we can connect you with an independent attorney in our network who can look at the details of your injury, explain how workers' comp interacts with any third-party liability, and help you understand what steps make sense next. There's no cost to you for this connection, and no obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why Brea Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Help You Look Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: California law usually makes workers' comp your exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker may still owe you separately. An independent attorney can help sort out whether that applies to your situation.

items.title: We Understand Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California requires injured workers to report the incident to their employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate a claim. Getting matched with an attorney quickly helps make sure nothing falls through the cracks.

items.title: We Know Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: Some injured workers worry that reporting an injury or filing a claim will cost them their job. California law prohibits employer retaliation for exercising these rights, and an attorney can help you understand your protections.

items.question: I was hurt at a warehouse near SR-57 in Brea — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' comp is your primary path against your employer regardless of fault, so that claim usually comes first. But if a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker played a role in the accident, you may also have a separate third-party claim. An independent attorney can review the details and explain which options apply to your case.

items.question: How long do I have to report my workplace injury in California?
items.answer: You generally need to notify your employer within 30 days of the injury to preserve your workers' comp rights. Waiting too long can make it harder to establish that the injury happened at work. If you're unsure whether you've missed this window, it's worth getting a quick review from an attorney.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workers' comp claim in Brea?
items.answer: No — California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim. If you believe you're facing retaliation, that itself may be worth discussing with an independent attorney. LawProactive can help connect you with someone who handles these situations.
